Subject: Fusion Labs — Execution timetable & reserve commitment (MAP draft)

Hi Anika —

Thanks for the call earlier. Attached is a first-pass Mutual Action Plan (MAP) and an execution timetable that aligns evaluation milestones with capacity reservation options (Dedicated vs Private). High-level ask: if Fusion Labs can confirm a capacity commitment by Oct 20 we can target a December go-live window with an initial dedicated pool. If you need on-prem/private options we can run an accelerated packaging track but lead times shift.

Key pieces in the draft:
- Evaluation sprint: 2 weeks (pilot workload, 3 test prompts, perf & quality gates) — owner: Fusion/Redwood
- Canaries: 2-node H100 canary for early traffic testing
- Initial production pool: recommend 6 x H100 equivalent (4 prod + 2 surge/canary) based on your 50–70 QPS estimate — see sizing sheet attached
- Procurement lead time: ~10–14 weeks for dedicated H100 reservations; Dedicated-hosted provisioning often completes in 4–6 weeks if we use available cloud tranches
- Private (on-prem) packaging: ~6–8 weeks for packaging + customer site prep; hardware procurement still on Fusion’s timeline

Open items for your team:
1) Final QPS and median prompt length to use for sizing (we used 1.2k tokens/session in the spreadsheet)
2) Decision point for Dedicated vs Private by Oct 20 to keep December ramp realistic
3) SOC2 / compliance checkpoint — we can provide SOC2 artifacts (attached summary)

Attachments: MAP-draft-v1.pdf (ownerable milestones), fusion-sizing-v2.xlsx (token/QPS assumptions), SOC2-summary.pdf

Next step: If you’re comfortable I’ll loop in Laura from Solutions to scope market/ops handoff and Priyom to lock the mutual acceptance criteria.

Thanks —
Ben

Ben —

Appreciate the quick turnaround and the MAP draft. A few clarifying questions before we convene internally:

- Procurement lead time: you noted 10–14 weeks for H100 reservations. If the hardware slips, what are our fallback patterns? Can we run with A100 (quantized) temporarily and then swap to H100 when nodes arrive?
- For the private deployment option: does Redwood provide an air-gapped installer or do we need a systems integrator? What are the typical resource requirements on our side?
- Sizing: we expected peak of ~60 QPS but our median prompt length is closer to 800 tokens. Can you re-run that worksheet with 800 tokens and include an optimistic lane (4 x H100) vs conservative lane (8 x H100)?
- Compliance: procurement wants the SOC2 artifacts and a short summary PDF — we saw it in attachments, thank you.

We’re planning an internal alignment meeting on Oct 12. If we get a clear option and runbook then procurement can aim to sign by Oct 20, but that depends on how the fallback to alternate HW looks.

Thanks,
Anika
Director, Platform Engineering, Fusion Labs
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Fusion Labs — Execution timetable & reserve commitment (MAP draft)

Hi Anika and team —

Thanks — I re-ran the sizing with your median of 800 tokens and put optimistic / conservative lanes into fusion-sizing-v2.xlsx (attached in my reply to Ben). Summary below:

Assumptions we used:
- 60 QPS sustained traffic profile; p95 token length = 800 tokens; batching optimized for low latency (target 120–180 ms p95)
- Model: Llama-3-class 70B equivalent (latency profile used in sizing)

Sizing lanes (latency / throughput estimates are rough; final numbers come after pilot):
- Optimistic lane (4 x H100 equivalent): supports ~40–60 QPS with careful batching and KV caching; p95 latency ~150–220 ms
- Baseline lane (6 x H100 equivalent): supports ~60–90 QPS; p95 latency ~120–180 ms
- Conservative lane (8 x H100 equivalent): supports headroom for burst (100+ QPS) and easy rollouts

Fallbacks / procurement patterns:
- Short-term fallback: deploy A100 quantized variant on Dedicated for first 6–8 weeks; expect 20–30% slower per-token and some quality delta. This requires model-variant acceptance in the MAP (we can add an explicit quality gate).
- Staged migration: start with a small Dedicated pool (2–3 nodes) as a canary, then expand reserved pool as H100 inventory becomes available. Redwood’s routing supports automatic fallback to the quantized variant when H100 capacity not available.

Private/on-prem notes:
- We provide an appliance-style package (installer + deployment runbook). For a typical private deployment: 2–3 infra engineers on your side for initial install and networking, plus access to an internal NFS or S3-compatible object store. Packaging track adds ~6 weeks to the timeline but gives you full control of hardware timelines.

I attached fusion-sizing-v2.xlsx with the lane rows and a cost delta estimate between lanes. Priyom — I copied you for the operational handoff and rollout SKUs.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer | Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

- Quality gate review (pass/fail): Redwood/ Fusion — Nov 2 — Owner: Redwood (Karthik)
- Contract & reservation signature: Procurement (Fusion) — Oct 20 — Owner: Fusion procurement
- Provision Dedicated canary pool (2 nodes): Redwood Ops — Nov 8 — Owner: Redwood (Priyom)
- Provision full reserved pool per lane: Redwood Ops — depends on lane (if H100 reserved, target complete by mid-December) — Owner: Redwood Ops
- Private packaging run (optional): if selected, kick on Oct 22, completion ~6 weeks later — Owner: Redwood (Laura)

Open asks for Fusion today:
1) Confirm lane (Optimistic / Baseline / Conservative) so we can publish SKU/commit numbers into the contract
2) Confirm whether you need an initial A100 fallback variant included in the MAP
3) Procurement contact for DocuSign — we can send a redline-ready addendum and a DocuSign link (https://docusign.com/FD-1789)

I’ll attach a one-page MAP summary to the DocuSign email and move the larger MAP into shared Drive for tracking. Priyom/Laura will follow with a short ops handoff doc and kickoff calendar invite once Fusion confirms lane choice.

Thanks — looking forward to aligning this week.

Ben
